chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyād and Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān all together, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Naṣr ibn Muzāḥim, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Jarrāḥ ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Rāfiʿ ibn Salamah, who said:

I was with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ṣalawātu Allāhi ʿalayhi, on the day of al-Nahrawān. While ʿAlī عليه السلام was sitting, a horseman came and said, “Peace be upon you, O ʿAlī.” So ʿAlī عليه السلام said to him, “And upon you be peace. What is the matter with you—may your mother be bereft of you—that you did not greet me as Amīr al-Muʾminīn?”

He said, “Yes, I shall inform you about that. I was with you when you were upon the truth at Ṣiffīn. But when you appointed the two arbiters, I dissociated myself from you and called you a mushrik. Then I came to not know where I should direct my wilayah. By Allah, for me to know your guidance from your misguidance is more beloved to me than the world and all that is in it.” So ʿAlī عليه السلام said to him, “May your mother be bereft of you, stand near me and I will show you the signs of guidance from the signs of misguidance.” So the man stood near him.

While he was like that, a horseman came galloping until he reached ʿAlī عليه السلام and said, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, receive glad tidings of victory. May Allah gladden your eye. By Allah, the people have all been killed.” He said to him, “On this side of the river or beyond it?” He said, “Rather, on this side of it.” He said, “You have lied. By the One who split the grain and created the soul, they will never cross until they are killed.” The man said, “So my insight concerning him increased.”

Then another came galloping on his horse and said the like of that to him, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام replied to him with the like of what he had replied to his companion. The doubting man said, “I even thought of charging at ʿAlī عليه السلام and splitting his head with the sword.”

Then two horsemen came galloping, their horses drenched in sweat, and they said, “May Allah gladden your eye, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn. Receive glad tidings of victory. By Allah, the people have all been killed.” ʿAlī عليه السلام said, “Was it beyond the river or on this side of it?” They said, “No, rather beyond it. When they drove their horses into al-Nahrawān and the water struck the upper chests of their horses, they turned back and were struck down.” So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said, “You two have spoken the truth.” Then the man dismounted from his horse, took hold of the hand and foot of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and kissed them. Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said, “This is a sign for you.”

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام as Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.إِمْرَةِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the authority and leadership of the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.الْحَقِّ: the truth upon which Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام stood
key_terms.عَلَامَاتِ الْهُدَى: the distinguishing signs of true guidance
key_terms.وَلَايَتِي: one’s allegiance and wilayah toward the rightful authority

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام demonstrate a sign of his true guidance at the battle of al-Nahrawān?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts an incident at al-Nahrawān in which a doubtful man sought to distinguish the guidance of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام from misguidance. Through foreknowledge of the battle’s outcome, Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام showed him a clear sign, leading the man to certainty regarding his wilayah and truthfulness.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Hassan, altogether from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Nasr Bin Muzahim, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Jarrah Bin Abdullah, from Rafie Bin Salama who said,

‘I was with Ali<sup>asws </sup>Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> on the Day of (the battle of) Al-Nahrawan. So while we were seated with Ali<sup>azwj</sup>, a horseman came over and he said, ‘Greetings be upon you<sup>asws</sup>, O Ali<sup>asws</sup>!’ So Ali<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘And upon you be the greetings! What is the matter with you, may your mother be bereft of you, you are not greeting upon me<sup>asws</sup> as Amir Al-Momineen?’

He said, ‘Yes, I shall inform you<sup>asws</sup> about that. I was, when you<sup>asws</sup> were upon the Truth at (the battle of) Siffeen. So when you<sup>asws</sup> made two judges to judge, I disavowed from you<sup>asws</sup> and called you<sup>asws</sup> a Polytheist. So I have become such that I do not know to where I should expend my guardianship. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! If I could recognise your<sup>asws</sup> Guidance from your<sup>asws</sup> straying, it would be more beloved to me than the world and whatever is in it’. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘May your mother be bereft of you! Pause closer to me<sup>asws</sup> and I<sup>asws</sup> shall show you signs of the Guidance from the signs of the straying’. So the man paused near to him<sup>asws</sup>’.

So while he was like that when a horseman came running until he came over to Ali<sup>asws</sup> and he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! Receive the good news of the victory. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> had Delighted your<sup>asws</sup> eyes. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! The group of people have been killed, altogether!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘From besides the river or from behind it?’ He said, ‘But, from besides it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You are lying! By the One<sup>azwj</sup> Whom Splits the seed and Forms the person (in the womb)! They will not be crossing the river ever, until they are killed’. So the man (first horseman) said, ‘So my insight has increased in it’.

So another one came to him<sup>asws</sup> galloping upon a horse, similar to that. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> responded to him similar to that which he<sup>asws</sup> had responded to his companions. The man (first horseman) said, ‘(At that point) I doubted and thought of attacking upon Ali<sup>asws</sup> and split his<sup>asws</sup> head with the sword’.

Then two horse-men came galloping, their two horses perspiring, and they both said, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Delighted your<sup>asws</sup> eyes, O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! Receive good news of the victory. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! The group of the people have been killed, altogether’. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Was it from behind the river or from besides it?’ They said, ‘No, but from behind it. They, when they stormed their horses into the Nahrwan and the water struck the manes of their cavalry horses, they returned, so they were hit’. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You two are speaking the truth’. So the man descended from his horse and grabbed the hand of Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>asws</sup> leg and kissed them. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is a sign for you!’
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and abu Ali al-Ash‘ari from Muhammad ibn Hassa’n, all of them from Muhammad ibn Ali, Nasr ibn Muzahim from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Jarrah ibn ‘Abdallah from Rafi‘ ibn Salama who has said the following.

“ On the day of al-Nahrawan I was in the presence of Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.). As we were sitting with the Imam (a.s.) a horse man approached and said, “al-salamu ‘Alayka ya Ali (peace be with you O Ali).” Ali (a.s.) said, “’Alayka al-salam (with you also be peace). May your mother weep over your dead body, why did you not addressed me as the Leader with Divine Authority?”

He said, “Yes, I like to inform you about it. I was present in al-Siffin when the truth was on your side. However, when approved the arbitrator to settle the warring parties I disregarded you and I called a polytheist. Ever since I do not know where should I turn to pledge allegiance to the Leadership with Divine Authority. If I can find a way to know whether you are on the right side or on wrong side it will be better for me than the world and all that is therein.” Ali (a.s.) said to him, “May your mother weep on your dead body. Come and stand up near me I will show the signs of the right and the signs of the wrong side.

As the man stood near him, a horse man approached running until he came to Ali (a.s.) and said, “O Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.), I have the glad news of victory. May Allah make it brightness to your eyes (out of joy). It is certain, by Allah, that all men of the enemy are killed.” Ali (a.s.) asked him, “Did it happen before or after their crossing the river?” He said, “Before or after crossing.” Ali (a.s.) said, “You have lied. I swear by the One Who makes the seed to germinate and causes the fetuses to develop, that they (enemy) will never cross the river until they are all killed.” The man has said that it added to my understanding.”

Another horse man came running and said just as what the one before had said and Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) refused to accept his words as those of the one before. The man who had doubts about Ali (a.s.) has said that he wanted to attack Ali (a.s.) with his sword and chop his head with the sword.

Two other men came running on horses soaked in sweet. They said, “May Allah brighten your eyes with the joy of victory O Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.). We have the glad news of victory for you. It is certain, by Allah, thatall of the people are killed.” Ali (a.s.) then asked, “Did it happen before or after their crossing the river?” They said, “It happened before their crossing the river. When they tried to cross it and water reached up to the mane of their horses they turned back and there they all were killed.” Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) said, “You have spoken the truth.” The man then climbed down his horse and held Amir al-Mu’minin’s (a.s.) hand and feet and kissed them.” Ali (a.s.) said, “This is the sign (my being on the right side for you) for you.”
